steps.title: Game rules
steps.body: Logic is what makes a map a game: when something happens (an event), do something (actions), maybe only if a condition holds. You can write it as a node graph or as code — they stay in sync.

steps.title: A new graph
steps.body: A project can have many graphs; each holds one or more event chains. + New makes a graph that starts with On start.
steps.task: Make a new logic graph (Graphs › + New).

steps.title: Add a node
steps.body: The palette lists every node by category: events (teal), flow (purple), variables, maths, world actions, audio, screens and cinematics. Click one to add it; search finds it by name.
steps.task: Add a Give item node from the palette.

steps.title: Wire it up
steps.body: Drag from a node's output pin to another node's input pin. White diamonds carry the flow (then → in); coloured circles carry values. Wrong types are refused with a tooltip.
steps.task: Connect On start's “then” to Give item's “in”.

steps.title: Graph or code
steps.body: Code shows the same graph as a few lines of JavaScript-like script; edit either and the other follows. Split shows both side by side. F9 on a node sets a breakpoint that pauses Play there.

steps.title: Variables
steps.body: Variables remember things while playing: a score, coins found, hearts. Logic reads and changes them; screens and signs show them with {name}.
